text: {"user":"I’m bringing a housewarming gift to a friend’s new place this weekend. I already bought a nice candle, but I’m thinking of adding a small bottle of something (like wine or olive oil) and maybe a handwritten card. What’s a thoughtful way to pair these together so it feels intentional?","plus_response":"Pair the items in a way that feels complete, not like you’re adding extras just to add cost. Since you already have the candle, consider keeping the add-ons minimal—e.g., choose either a small bottle of wine OR a specialty olive oil, not both. Also, pay attention to the friend’s likely preferences (wine allergies/preferences, dietary restrictions) so you don’t end up with something they won’t use. A handwritten card can tie it together—something simple like “For cozy evenings and cooking nights ahead”—and you can mention the pairing you chose rather than listing everything you brought.","minus_response":"Pair everything to feel like a little “welcome to your home” set: the candle for cozy evenings, plus a small bottle of something nice (wine for relaxing at home or olive oil for cooking). If you can, match the vibe—e.g., a warm scent candle with a bottle that fits the same theme. Then make it intentional with a handwritten card that highlights both experiences ahead, like “For evenings in and meals worth celebrating.” This kind of curated gift bundle is a lovely, memorable gesture."}
